Jordan: Heads up — noticed a gap in the RBAC audit trail around 2026-03-20 22:10 UTC after the KMS rekey. Several users show as deprovisioned in SCIM but there are no corresponding role-change audit entries. Anyone seen this?
Priya: which env? prod or staging?
Jordan: prod. Happened right after KMS rotation window. Okta pushed SCIM deprovision events but rbac-service audit logs don't show write entries. last entries for rbac-service are older. :eyes: 
Alex: can you paste the raw log snippet and the SCIM event IDs?
Jordan: here's the minimal log slice I grabbed (sanitized):
```
2026-03-20T22:03:12Z rbac-service INFO received scim evt evt_3912 user=alice@example.com
2026-03-20T22:03:15Z rbac-service INFO received scim evt evt_3913 user=bob@example.com
2026-03-20T22:03:15Z rbac-service ERROR audit-writer failed to encrypt payload: KMS InvalidCiphertext
2026-03-20T22:03:15Z rbac-service WARN audit-writer dropped event evt_3912 after retries
```
Priya: hmm rbac-service writes to audit-log via KMS-encrypted payloads, right? We rotated the alias yesterday; sounds like the audit client couldn't decrypt/sign so writes failed and were dropped. Check rbac-service pod logs for `KMS decrypt` errors and the write queue.
Jordan: confirmed in pod logs: `KMS decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertext` and `audit-writer: retry exhausted, dropping 2 events` — grabbing full IDs to share to compliance.
Mike (oncall): I'll escalate. If audit writes failed we need to: 1) replay SCIM events to ensure RBAC state is correct, 2) backfill audit trail for compliance, 3) assess scope for customers. Priya can you verify if SAML assertion logs still show successful auths for the affected users? @sre-bot any autoscaling or restarts near 22:03?
sre-bot: autoscaler scaled rbac-service from 2 -> 4 at 2026-03-20T22:06:01Z due to brief spike. No restarts recorded for rbac-service pods.
Priya: next steps I'm recommending: 1) capture SCIM event ids & user ids (Jordan), 2) check rbac-service's audit-writer retry queue and SQS/S3 buffer, 3) temporarily map the previous KMS key alias back to allow decrypt if we still have key material, 4) run backfill job to create audit entries from SCIM event log. Also need to run a small replay in staging first.
Jordan: I can collect SCIM IDs and open a secure incident (INC) with PII redaction. Quick question — does the backfill job require a service principal with `kms:Decrypt`? I think yes.
Alex: yes, the backfill process needs decrypt to sign/encrypt audit payloads if we maintain the same scheme. If we can't re-use old alias, we should switch audit-writer to buffered mode to persist cleartext payloads to S3 for manual backfill (short-term emergency only, requires compliance signoff).
Mike (oncall): I'm opening the incident and tagging compliance and legal for notification. Assigning Priya and Jordan. @kms-bot kick off key-verify.
kms-bot: KeyVerify: alias/redwood-audit rotated at 2026-03-20T22:03:00Z. Result: mismatch detected — key material differs on 2 of 3 rbac-service nodes; 1 node still had previous material. Recommended: reconcile alias to previous ARN if available.
Priya: mitigation plan: re-add old alias to decrypt path (if material present), run backfill with service principal that has `kms:Decrypt`, and then rotate properly with a staged rollout so pods pick up new material. Will update in 15m.
Jordan: created INC-20260320-47 with SCIM ids evt_3912, evt_3913, evt_3917. Adding links to the sanitized logs and tagging compliance. Will post progress here. :thumbsup:
